My daughter has a condition that requires two variations of the same medication, delivered by different methods. These are clearly described on her prescription, and I consistently order the same items each time. Despite this, the surgery repeatedly approves the incorrect version. This inevitably results in a phone call to the surgery — a process I dread.

Each time I call, I am met with reception staff who are cold, unhelpful, and show very little understanding or compassion. Today, I was told that the solution would be to remove one of the medications from his prescription — even though both are essential. I do not understand what authority a receptionist has to question or override a patient’s established medication needs.

I understand that working on reception in a busy GP surgery is not easy, and that staff must deal with a wide range of people. However, the consistent lack of empathy and professionalism suggests a systemic issue with the surgery’s approach to patient care. People usually contact their GP in a moment of need. Being met with rudeness or indifference only adds stress to what is already a difficult situation.

I hope this feedback is taken seriously and that steps are taken to improve the training and support provided to front-of-house staff.
